lane: Billing lot 2: the Android app buys and restores Premium through Google Play (RevenueCat SDK)
goal: Let a signed-in Android user buy or restore the one Premium plan (monthly or annual) through Google Play Billing via the react-native-purchases SDK, with the RevenueCat app user id equal to the Supabase user id so the lot 1 webhook can write public.subscriptions. The app shows store prices only (no hard-coded VND), a dynamic annual saving, an honest paywall (plan, total charged, period, auto-renew, how to cancel, restore, terms and privacy) and merges CustomerInfo with the user's own subscriptions row using the same rule as the server. premiumOnSale stays false: the paywall is visible to ordinary users only when Premium is on sale, or in a build with EXPO_PUBLIC_BILLING_TEST=true for closed-test purchase trials.
successCriteria: react-native-purchases 10.16.0 is a dependency of apps/mobile only (10.x per the SDK 11.0.0 note that Expo apps should stay on 10.x; it ships Play Billing Library 8.3.0); com.android.vending.BILLING is declared in both app.json and the committed AndroidManifest.xml; versionCode and versionName are unchanged.

runtimeConfig exposes the public SDK key EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_ANDROID_KEY and the build flag EXPO_PUBLIC_BILLING_TEST (off by default); with no key, on web, in Expo Go or without the native module, billing reports unavailable and the app runs normally.

billingClient configures once, logs in with the Supabase user id before any purchase, never purchases when signed out, treats a user cancel as no error, and maps network, store, already-owned and pending errors to friendly Vietnamese/English messages without technical detail.

usePremium merges an active CustomerInfo premium entitlement with the user's own subscriptions rows (premium or legacy premium_astrology_ai; same status and period rule as supabase/functions/_shared/premium-entitlement.ts), polls the row for about 30 seconds after a purchase, keeps the last known value offline and fails closed with no data.

PaywallPanel renders loading, unavailable, plan choice, purchasing, pending, error and already-Premium states with store priceString, a dynamic annual saving shown only when cheaper, Manage plan (Google Play subscriptions), Restore purchases, terms and privacy links, accessibility labels and 44 pt touch targets; no user-facing text names the vendor.

resolveAccountTier accepts entitled; App.tsx uses usePremium for the account tier; the Premium buttons in AiDeepRead and AstrologyExperience open the Premium section; ordinary users no longer see the 99.000/799.000 VND hypothesis.
tsc, the full mobile jest suite, mobile:release:config:check, validate:governance and this preflight pass.
untouchedSurfaces: packages/agent-config/account-tier-policy.json keeps premiumOnSale false and mode unchanged; EXPO_PUBLIC_BILLING_TEST only shows the paywall and never changes the tier.
supabase/ is untouched: no SQL, no RLS change, no Edge Function change or deploy; the server stays the authority for Astrology AI.
No EAS build, no store release, no versionCode or versionName change; no key value is written to the repository and no .env file is read.
PLAN.md is updated by the lead agent; legal pages, Data safety and account deletion are lot 3.

impact.entryPoint: Profile > Premium section (PaywallPanel), Premium buttons in the Astrology deep read and AI guide, account tier in App.tsx.
impact.dataWrite: No database write by the app. Google Play and RevenueCat record purchases; the lot 1 webhook writes public.subscriptions after an approved deploy. The app only reads its own subscriptions rows under the existing RLS.
impact.backendContract: New read of public.subscriptions (entitlement, status, current_period_end) for the signed-in user; no Edge Function contract change.
impact.privacySafety: Only the Supabase user id is sent to the billing SDK as the app user id; no email, birth data or content. Payment details stay with Google Play.
impact.observability: No new logging; SDK log level stays default and errors are mapped to codes without technical text on screen.
impact.rollback: Revert the commit and rebuild the native app; with no SDK key in the build, billing is already inert.

canonicalContracts: RevenueCat entitlement premium, default offering packages $rc_monthly and $rc_annual

skillReview.name: nilaza-plan-qc
skillReview.evidence: Record and preflight before code; Owner decisions of 15/11 applied (one plan, store prices, premiumOnSale false); release, secrets and settings left to the Owner.

dependencyReview.evidence: Billing SDK install, Expo support, error codes and Play Billing Library version change often; checked against current vendor docs, the 11.0.0 release note and the published package metadata on 2026-11-15.

externalSourceReview.reason: Expo install needs a development build (expo-dev-client); Expo Go runs a mock preview mode, so real purchases need a native build.
11.x needs RN 0.80, Kotlin 2.1, Play Billing 9.1 and says Expo apps should stay on 10.x for now; 10.16.0 chosen.
10.16.0 ships purchases-android 10.30.0 with Google Play Billing Library 8.3.0.
logIn with the backend user id before purchase so the webhook app_user_id is the Supabase user id; logOut on sign-out.

securityReview.authzRls: The app reads only its own public.subscriptions rows with the user's token under the existing select-own RLS; it never writes them. Purchase requires a signed-in Supabase account and a completed SDK logIn with that id.
securityReview.sensitiveData: Only the Supabase user id goes to the SDK; card and payment data stay with Google Play.
securityReview.secretsLogging: EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_ANDROID_KEY is the public SDK key, set per EAS environment by the Owner, never committed; no secret is placed in an EXPO_PUBLIC variable and no key value is logged.
securityReview.externalInput: Offering, price strings and CustomerInfo come from the store SDK and are shown as text only; subscription rows are validated by the shared rule and fail closed.
securityReview.dependencies: Adds react-native-purchases 10.16.0 (MIT, RevenueCat) to apps/mobile: the vendor SDK for Google Play Billing chosen by the Owner in the billing plan; it pulls @revenuecat/purchases-typescript-internal and purchases-js-hybrid-mappings 19.17.0 (plus @revenuecat/purchases-js 1.73.1 transitively, used only by the SDK's browser mode, which Nilaza never loads) and the native purchases-android 10.30.0 with Play Billing 8.3.0.
securityReview.migrationRelease: No SQL and no deploy. A native rebuild (EAS) and the Owner's SDK key are needed before any purchase can be tried; that build and any release need Owner approval.
securityReview.stopCondition: Stop if tsc or a mobile test fails, if the BILLING permission cannot be declared, or if the SDK cannot be imported safely on web and in tests.

workingTreeReview.note: Record and preflight came first; these are the Lot 2 edits, all inside writeScope. sourceReview hashes refreshed after editing.

managerTestPath: In a closed-test build with EXPO_PUBLIC_BILLING_TEST=true and the SDK key: sign in, open Profile > Premium, see the monthly and annual store prices, buy one as a license tester, see 'activating' then Premium; reinstall, sign in and tap Restore purchases.
residualRisk: Nothing has been tried on a device or against Google Play yet. The webhook (lot 1) is not deployed, so after a purchase the app unlocks from CustomerInfo but the server keeps refusing Astrology AI until the row exists. Payment through Vietnamese carriers or wallets is unverified.
